takeaway: The medial border of the femoral ring is the lacunar ligament. Lateral: femoral vein; anterior: inguinal ligament; posterior: pectineal ligament.

question.text: Which one of the following structures forms the medial border of the femoral ring?

lines.text: The femoral ring is the doorway at the top of the femoral canal, guarded on four sides.
On the medial side stands the lacunar ligament, the glowing curtain.
Laterally is the femoral vein, the blue knight with his shield.
In front, the inguinal ligament forms the rope bridge.
Behind, the pectineal ligament is the solid stone wall.
So the medial border is the lacunar ligament.
From lateral to medial, the femoral structures spell NAVY: nerve, artery, vein, lymph nodes.
